source_method: Web-verified public parish, government, heritage and local reporting pages checked 21 Oct 2026; titles and claim scopes corrected; no app publishing.

records.french_name: Herbergsuche — dévotion locale de l'hospitalité pendant l'Avent
records.claim: The Roman Catholic parish of Großpetersdorf documents a house-to-house Advent tradition in which an image or statue of Mary passes from family to family with prayers. Local Advent calendars and parish programmes vary.
records.calendar: Advent; individual parish house-visit itinerary, not a universal fixed nine-day programme

sources.supports: House-to-house passage of Marian image or statue, household devotion, connection with Mary and Joseph seeking lodging
sources.limit: 2023 parish witness; does not prove every German-speaking parish celebrates on the same dates.

limits: The local Austrian house-visit devotion is not identical to Mexican Las Posadas.
Neither a universal 15–23 December date range nor a fixed nine-day requirement is substantiated by this parish witness.

records.english_name: La guignolée — French Canadian Christmas alms collection
records.french_name: La guignolée — quête caritative canadienne-française de Noël
records.claim: The Québec cultural heritage register independently identifies guignolée charitable food collections initiated by the Society of St Vincent de Paul in the early 1860s. The Montréal Society's current page confirms continued local Christmas-season campaigns.
records.calendar: Christmas-season charity drive; actual annual dates locally announced

sources.issuer: Québec Répertoire du patrimoine culturel — La guignolée
sources.supports: Charitable Catholic origins in early 1860s and historical door-to-door donation collection
sources.limit: Museum artifact account: does not specify universal current parish practice.

sources.issuer: Société de Saint-Vincent de Paul de Montréal
sources.supports: 2026 official organizer account of ongoing guignolée and local December collection
sources.limit: Modern collection may include non-Catholic participants and is not a universal liturgical act.

limits: Later nonreligious charitable collections do not automatically retain explicit Catholic religious character.
Do not invent universal collection days, donations or parish participation.

records.french_name: Kolędnicy polonais — quêteurs et chanteurs de Noël
records.claim: Poland's official educational portal describes kolędnicy who visit households, sing carols and sometimes stage Nativity or Herod plays, preserving a distinction between religious singing and wider folk theatre.
records.calendar: Christmas cycle; dates and troupe forms differ across regions

sources.issuer: Polish government educational portal ZPE — Polskie obyczaje bożonarodzeniowe
sources.supports: Definition of Christmas house-to-house carollers, performances and greetings
sources.limit: Educational/ethnographic description, not certification of a specifically Roman Catholic ritual or date.

limits: Some performances contain secular folklore; not all forms are explicitly Catholic rites.
Do not conflate Polish groups with German Epiphany Sternsinger or Hungarian Bethlehem play.

records.claim: The Archdiocese of Vienna documents branches cut from cherry or apple trees and placed in water on St Barbara's 4 December observance, sometimes flowering by Christmas.
records.calendar: Traditional observance 4 December; voluntary domestic symbolism, not a Mass rite

sources.issuer: Archdiocese of Vienna — St Barbara, 4 December
sources.supports: Exact 4 December domestic branch custom, winter flowering and association with the saint's legend
sources.limit: Blooming is not guaranteed and the legend is not established biography.

limits: The natural bloom is horticultural, not a guaranteed divine sign.
Does not establish obligatory plant species or universal liturgical use.

records.english_name: L-Irxoxt — Maltese running procession with the Risen Christ
records.french_name: L-Irxoxt — procession maltaise du Ressuscité portée au pas de course
records.claim: Malta's public administration documents the traditional Easter Sunday L-Irxoxt procession, and contemporary reporting directly witnesses local runs with statues of the risen Christ.
records.geo: Malta and Gozo, confirmed in named communities
records.calendar: Easter Sunday, only parishes with actual announced procession

sources.supports: Traditional L-Irxoxt Resurrection procession as Easter Sunday custom
Observed statue-running in Senglea and Three Cities on Easter Sunday

limits: The Malta government source confirms a Resurrection procession in Gozo, not the act of running the statue.
Times of Malta documents actual statue runs in specific localities, notably Senglea and the Three Cities; the practice is not identical in every parish.
Do not use the local celebration to infer any action within the 1962 Mass.

records.english_name: Faradda di li Candareri — Sassari's Marian offering procession
records.french_name: Faradda di li Candareri — procession votive mariale de Sassari
records.claim: Sassari's municipal programme confirms its annual 14 August guild procession carrying decorated wooden votive candles to Santa Maria di Betlem, and Italy's Ministry of Culture registers the Faradda as a distinct local August Marian heritage tradition.
records.calendar: 14 August local procession associated with Assumption, not a universal Marian vigil rite

sources.supports: Local event, 14 August in 2026, procession to Santa Maria di Betlem
sources.limit: Specific 2026 local programme, not a transferable liturgical calendar event.

sources.issuer: Italian Ministry of Culture heritage registry
sources.supports: Annual 14 August Marian votive procession and history
sources.limit: Medieval origin narratives require separate documentary analysis.

limits: It is a Sassari-specific votive procession, not a universal Assumption rite.
Do not fix the number of candelieri from older contradictory museum descriptions; the 2026 municipal festival site describes thirteen.
The feast date does not imply a procession in any other parish.
